name: Machine Seated Calf Raise
grip: Hands holding stability handles or the release lever beside the thigh pads.
description: Perform bilateral ankle plantar flexion against padded thigh supports while seated with knees bent to 90 degrees, biomechanically unloading the gastrocnemius to isolate the soleus.
setup: Sit on the machine and place the balls of both feet on the lower edge of the footplate with heels hanging freely.
Adjust and secure the padded thigh lever snugly across your lower thighs just above your knees.
Disengage the safety support release bar and allow your heels to lower into full ankle dorsiflexion.
instructions: Lower your heels down into a deep, comfortable stretch below the footplate level.
Press forcefully through the balls of both feet into full plantar flexion, driving the thigh pad upward onto your tiptoes.
Hold the peak contraction at the top for a count of one, squeezing the deep calf muscles.
Lower slowly under complete control back into the full bottom stretch before beginning the next repetition.
Re-engage the safety catch lever when the set is finished.
cues: Drop heels deep for a loaded stretch.
Press high onto the balls of the feet.
Pause at both the stretch and the top.
commonMistakes: Bouncing rapidly out of the bottom stretch using Achilles tendon elasticity instead of muscular contraction.
Cutting the range of motion short.
Placing the thigh pads too high on the upper thighs instead of just above the knees.

logging.example: Two 20 kg plates loaded on horn: record 40 kg total plate load.
logging.note: Most seated calf raise machines are plate-loaded lever arms; record the total mass of weight plates loaded.

variantNote: Bent-knee calf raise. Flexing the knee to 90 degrees causes active insufficiency of the biarticular gastrocnemius, isolating the monoarticular soleus under direct load.
